description: Godna is an ancient tattoo and drawing tradition of the Mithila region, later adapted into a distinctive style of Madhubani painting using fine dotted lines.
why_it_matters: Godna preserves motifs and a visual language older than paper-based Madhubani, and gave lower-caste women artists their own recognised style.
status_note: Documented as practised by fewer artists today as demand shifts to mainstream Madhubani styles. BharatVerse presents this as contextual demo content, not an official endangerment listing.

description: The Manganiyar and Langa are hereditary communities of professional folk musicians in western Rajasthan, performing centuries-old repertoire on the kamaicha, sarangi and dholak.
why_it_matters: Their oral repertoire encodes genealogy, history and Sufi-bhakti poetry of the desert, passed down without notation.
status_note: Community musicians report that younger generations increasingly leave the profession for other work. Presented as demo context, not an official listing.

description: Sujani is a narrative quilting-embroidery of Bihar in which old cloth is layered and stitched into story-telling coverlets depicting village life and social messages.
why_it_matters: Sujani is both a recycling craft and a rare women's storytelling medium addressing social themes; it carries a GI (Geographical Indication) tag.
status_note: Sustained by a small number of cooperatives. BharatVerse presents this as contextual demo content.

description: Kathputli is the traditional string-puppet theatre of Rajasthan, telling folk legends of kings and heroes with carved wooden puppets and live narration.
why_it_matters: One of the oldest forms of folk entertainment in India, it carries oral history and regional legend.
status_note: Puppeteer families report shrinking audiences and income. Presented as demo context, not an official endangerment listing.
